name: AT&T Home Phone (landline, AT&T Phone - Advanced/Digital Phone)
notes: Researched from public att.com support articles only (no sign-in). Sign-in uses an AT&T user ID, email address or wireless number on a two-step myAT&T sign-in; a one-time verification code is sent when signing in from a new browser or device (text to the AT&T wireless number; text or email during setup). Online payments accept debit/credit cards, Apple Pay and online banking; checking/savings accounts are available only when signed in. AutoPay is toggled On/Off on the AutoPay page and can draft a bank account, debit or credit card; card payments draft earlier than the due date, bank/debit closer to it, which the dossier cannot express (family default kept). AutoPay + paperless together earn a monthly discount on qualified plans (amount not published). Payment arrangements are made by picking a date after the due date on 'Schedule payment date'; arrangements made by phone/chat carry a convenience fee (amount not published). Cancelling Digital Phone/Phone - Advanced or a landline is by phone only. Plan prices are not modelled (not published on the pages used).

autopay_cancel.note: AutoPay cannot be turned off when your service or credit status requires automatic payments; removing it also removes AutoPay discounts.

cancel_service.note: Home phone cannot be cancelled online. Call 800.288.2020 for Digital Phone or Phone - Advanced; landline customers in some states call 800.288.2747. Only the account owner can cancel.

help.title: Ways to pay your AT&T bill
paragraphs: You can pay online, in person, by phone or by mail. Online, AT&T takes Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Discover, JCB and Diners Club debit or credit cards, Apple Pay, and online banking through PayWithMyBank where your bank participates.
Paying from a checking or savings account, an AT&T promotional card, BitPay or Mastercard Click to Pay is available only after you sign in to myAT&T.
Online payments usually post within minutes, but can take up to 24 hours.

help.title: Sign up for and manage AutoPay
paragraphs: Open AutoPay, sign in if asked, pick the account and switch AutoPay On, then follow the prompts. Repeat for each AT&T account. AutoPay can use a bank account, a debit card or a credit card.
Credit card AutoPay payments are drafted earlier than the due date; debit card and bank account payments are drafted closer to it.

To stop AutoPay, switch it Off on the same page. AutoPay cannot be stopped if your service or credit status requires automatic payments, and removing it also removes any AutoPay discount. You can pause AutoPay for one month, but you still need to pay by the due date.
steps: Open AutoPay and choose the account.
Choose your payment method and confirm.

help.title: Paperless billing
paragraphs: Open Paperless billing, confirm the account, select Change and choose to keep or cancel paperless billing, then verify your email address.

Having both AutoPay and paperless billing earns a monthly discount on qualified plans. If you cancel paperless billing, paper bills start arriving by mail within two billing periods. Some services and credit situations require paperless billing.

help.title: Make a payment arrangement
paragraphs: If you need more time, use Schedule payment date to see the payment calendar and pick an available date after your due date. If no later dates are offered, you are not eligible for an arrangement online.

The payment is taken from the method you chose on that date, starting at 12 a.m. Eastern. Arrangements and payments dated after the original due date cannot be changed or cancelled. Late fees still apply, a convenience fee applies if you set the arrangement up by calling or chatting with AT&T, and a reconnection fee applies if service is suspended because the date is missed.
If you use AutoPay, pause it for the current month; it resumes the next bill period.

help.title: Cancel AT&T home phone
paragraphs: Home phone service is cancelled by phone, not online. For AT&T Digital Phone, including Phone - Advanced, call 800.288.2020; AT&T can remove numbers, suspend or disconnect service, or move it to a new address. Service bought less than 14 days ago may qualify for an equipment return and refund.
For a traditional landline in the states where it applies, call 800.288.2747 to change or cancel. Only the account owner can cancel landline service.

help.title: Sign-in verification codes
paragraphs: Sign in with your AT&T user ID, email address or wireless number. AT&T sends a one-time verification code when you sign in from a new browser or device, after clearing cookies, with a different ID, or after a password reset.
When you create your user ID you can get the code by text, email, phone call or mail; text and email are fastest.

extra.intent: Using the AT&T website's support pages, find the phone number to call to cancel AT&T Phone - Advanced (Digital Phone) home phone service. Do not make a payment or change any settings.
